title: Mission
summary: These passages connect mission with blessing, witness, proclamation, and life among the nations. Genesis 12 says that blessing through Abraham will reach the families of the earth. Matthew 28 records Jesus sending disciples to make disciples among all nations; Acts 1 links witness to the Spirit’s power; Romans 15 describes Paul’s work among Gentiles; and 1 Peter 2 calls its readers to proclaim God’s deeds and live honorably among their neighbors. The passages share an outward direction but describe different roles and settings.
historical_context: The references range from the promise to Abraham in Genesis to post-resurrection instructions in Matthew, the disciples’ witness in Acts, Paul’s account of his work in Romans, and pastoral counsel in 1 Peter. This summary stays with the settings described by those texts; the source list does not support additional historical reconstruction.
canonical_context: Genesis frames blessing to the families of the earth as part of the promise to Abraham. In the New Testament references, Jesus sends disciples to all nations, Acts describes Spirit-empowered witness, Romans presents Paul’s Gentile ministry, and 1 Peter describes a community whose public conduct accompanies its proclamation. These passages connect divine blessing and witness without making every text describe the same mission task.
literary_context: The selected forms include a promise, a commission in a Gospel narrative, a programmatic statement in Acts, Paul’s first-person account of ministry, and a letter’s exhortation to a community. Those differences clarify who acts and how: God’s promise, Jesus’ sending, the Spirit’s empowerment, Paul’s work, and the community’s witness through speech and conduct.
covenantal_significance: Genesis 12 places blessing beyond Abraham’s family within the promise itself. Matthew, Acts, Romans, and 1 Peter show different New Testament expressions of outward witness: teaching and disciple-making, Spirit-empowered testimony, Paul’s Gentile ministry, and a community’s proclamation and public life. This connects mission with blessing while preserving the specific task assigned in each passage.
canonical_role: This entry connects the promise of blessing to the nations with several New Testament forms of witness. Its passages distinguish God’s promise, Jesus’ commission, the Spirit’s empowering, an apostle’s work, and a community’s public testimony.

interpretive_notes.note: Read Mission in its immediate context before generalizing.
Do not flatten distinct passages into one slogan; let the canon keep its own shape.
